extracted.intended_audience: government procurement officers, contracting attorneys, and contractors bidding on federal/War Department contracts
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and rules governing federal government invitations for bids, the advertisement requirement, bid formality waivers, bidder responsibility, award decisions (including lowest responsible bidder), and grounds for rejection or acceptance of bids under statutes and War Department regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior written authority for publication (section 3828)
rubrics_metrics.description: "No advertisement, notice, or proposal for any executive department ... shall be published in any newspaper whatever, except in pursuance of a written authority for such publication from the head of such department; and no bill for any such advertising or publication shall be paid unless there be presented with such bill a copy of such written authority."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The written authority required must precede the publication; a subsequent approval or ratification will not be sufficient. (C. 17990, May 13, 1906.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory advertising duty (section 3709) and its object
rubrics_metrics.description: Under section 3709, the duty of advertising is a legal obligation imposed by statute. The main object of advertising is to induce free and open competition and to protect the United States from fraudulent combinations and collusive preferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An advertisement also constitutes a pledge that, as a general rule, the contract will be awarded to the lowest responsible bidder provided he is responsible, his bid is reasonable, and he complies with existing regulations (bond, etc.). The reservation "reserves the right to reject any or all proposals" is precautionary and generally not exercised except for legal reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award not automatically to lowest bidder if not responsible/qualified
rubrics_metrics.description: The award should be to the lowest responsible bidder, but the statute does not require award to the lowest bidder where he cannot satisfy the department that he can furnish required quality and within required time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If facts leave reasonable doubt about quality/performance/time, award to the lowest bidder may be passed over for the next lowest satisfactory bidder. Considerations include available plant/facilities and relative efficiency of the goods (e.g., boilers with better fuel efficiency may justify higher bid). (C. 20276, Aug. 22, 1906; C. 25493, Aug. 28, 1909.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Reservation to reject any or all proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: An advertisement often includes the statement that the United States reserves the right to reject any or all proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reservation is precautionary; awards should normally be made to the lowest responsible bidder unless legal and proper conditions are not met. See Army Regulations paragraph language and cases cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to name manufacturer when bidder is not manufacturer
rubrics_metrics.description: Advertisements for supplies should instruct bidders who are not manufacturers to submit the name of the manufacturer from whom such goods are to be obtained, unless manifestly impracticable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance published in General Orders 167 (War Department, Oct. 10, 1905) for procurement officers; intended to enable evaluation of bidder capability and origin of goods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial standing and facilities as grounds for rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Lack of commercial standing on the part of the bidder or inadequate facilities or plant on the part of the manufacturer will constitute good and sufficient grounds for rejection of bids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abnormally low bids should be subjected to the strictest scrutiny and comparison with prevailing market rates to ensure responsibility and reasonableness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection for prior unjustified failure to perform
rubrics_metrics.description: All bids received from contractors who have failed unjustifiably to fill former contracts with the Government shall be rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General Order 167 directs rejection of such bidders, but what constitutes "failed unjustifiably" is fact-dependent; high-standing firms with limited prior lapses may not be excluded. An attempt to deliver inferior goods may not always constitute unjustified failure. (C. 29175; C. 28861.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Printing contracts must be awarded as full printing contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriation for printing must be expended on printing after due notice and competition; contracts should be given to the lowest responsible practical printer able to do the printing unaided by the Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is not compliance with the statute to purchase paper, ink, type, etc., and let by contract only the mere printing; the contractor should be able to perform the full printing work. (P. 61, 334, Sept. 14, 1893.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Guaranty and default remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutes authorize requiring a written guaranty that if a bidder defaults in entering into a contract and giving sufficient bond, the officer shall proceed to contract with another person and charge the difference against the bidder and his guarantor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a lowest responsible bidder defaults, the act of 1878 (as amended) authorizes contracting with another and charging the difference to the defaulting bidder; the acts do not require awarding to the next lowest bidder automatically. (C. 22567, Feb. 17, 1908.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of bids and exceptions for mail/messenger delays
rubrics_metrics.description: Where advertisement specified bids would be opened at certain hour, ordinarily bids received after that hour should not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions permit consideration if the bid was duly mailed in ample time or a messenger started in time and failure to arrive was not due to bidder's neglect and the bidder gained no unfair advantage. Courts and opinions have allowed late bids where mailed in time, returned for lack of postage then remailed without opening, telegraphed prices where mailed before opening, or where a messenger missed a train but no unfair advantage resulted. Narrow margins or failure to follow marking instructions, however, can justify rejection. (Multiple citations C. 20416 et seq.; par. 547 amendment described.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Bid omissions (check instead of bid, missing signature/stamps) may be cured if honest and no unfair advantage
rubrics_metrics.description: If a sealed envelope opened contained only the check and the bidder later produced the bid amount and it satisfactorily appeared omission was accidental and no advantage gained, the bid could be considered; failure to sign the bid may be cured where guaranty is properly executed or bidder communicates intent to stand by the bid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signatures and required internal-revenue stamps have been attached after opening where intent and guaranty indicate enforceability. (C. 11609; C. 10361; C. 23878.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample submission requirements and waiver of informality
rubrics_metrics.description: Where specifications require submission of samples before the time fixed for opening bids, the failure to file a sample may be an informality which can be waived if the bidder acts in good faith and the sample offered later meets specifications and bidder had prior performance history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: lowest bidder who omitted sample but offered one within an hour or two after opening and had previously furnished denim under contract — failure was held a waivable informality. (G. 25021, May 26, 1909.)

rubrics_metrics.name: "Or equal" bids and sample requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When bids are requested for items 'of a certain make "or equal,"' instructions requiring samples of proposed equivalents to accompany the proposal mean failure to furnish samples may be an informality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such informality can be waived; contracting officer may call for samples prior to making awards since doing so would not facilitate collusion nor be unfair to other bidders. Guarantors remain bound despite initial absence of samples. (C. 20196, Aug. 10, 1906.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple-interest/multiple-bid clause may be waived
rubrics_metrics.description: A clause providing that reasonable grounds for supposing any bidder is interested in more than one bid will be cause for rejection is not mandatory; the clause may be waived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interest referred to is as a bidder; being a manufacturer or seller to a bidder is not necessarily disqualifying. (C. 19967, June 26, 1906.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to attach specifications or required alternate/unit prices can be informality
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to attach a copy of the specifications or to submit required alternative bids/unit prices may be an informality which does not necessarily invalidate the bid where references in the bid make intent clear or where the requirement's purpose (e.g., budget contingency) is not implicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: reference to specifications in bid made attachment unnecessary; failure to submit alternative bids where lowest bid within appropriation was waivable; failure to state price for insignificant item (rock excavation) could be waived where intended to include it under miscellaneous item. (C. 23552; C. 24769; C. 28603.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to submit duplicates is a waivable informality
rubrics_metrics.description: Where proposals were invited in duplicate and lowest bidder submitted only one copy, the failure to submit bids in duplicate was held an informality which could be waived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readvertisement equals rejection of all prior bids
rubrics_metrics.description: A readvertisement of work is equivalent to a rejection of all bids not theretofore accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of one bid rejects all others; effects on guaranties
rubrics_metrics.description: The acceptance of one bid is a rejection of all other bids, and a rejected bid cannot be later accepted to hold a guarantor to his guaranty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejection of all bids releases guarantors; guaranties cannot be revived by a mere letter consenting to revival — proper way is to call for new bids accompanied by new guaranties. (C. 8904; C. 20670; C. 26846.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting officer discretion to determine 'lowest responsible bidder'
rubrics_metrics.description: A sound discretion is vested in the contracting officer, subject to higher approval, to determine whether a bidder is the 'lowest responsible bidder' in light of all circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facts such as attempts to deliver inferior articles, causing delays, or false charges against contracting officer may justify awarding to next lowest bidder. (C. 18166; C. 28861.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to reject bids for fraud or collusion
rubrics_metrics.description: The United States may properly reject a bid in case of fraud — e.g., where the lowest bidder is in collusion with other bidders or with a government representative to impose a high price.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bids of all bidders concerned in the fraud may be rejected even without specific regulation or statute. However, mere facts such as a bidder stating supplies will be made by a firm with a member previously disqualified do not automatically justify rejection absent stronger indicia of fraud. (R., 37, 564; C. 7134; C. 8606; C. 13485; C. 23552.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate/individual role facts do not automatically nullify bids
rubrics_metrics.description: Situations where individuals who are officers/directors of a company submitted separate bids and stated the company would manufacture if awarded do not necessarily amount to a fraud on the United States or justify rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if true that multiple individual bids are effectively for the same company, absence of clear fraudulent conspiracy or improper advantage means bids need not be rejected. (C. 27496, Nov. 16, 1910.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Bidders not entitled to government-supplied competitor prices
rubrics_metrics.description: A bidder is not entitled to be furnished by the War Department or its officers with the prices of other bidders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A bidder present at the opening may make memoranda; copies of any bid may be obtained from the returns office of the Interior Department under section 515, R. S. (C. 26895, June 18, 1910.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Option/quantity reservation language should be definite (Judge Advocate recommendation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard advertisement language reserving the right to make orders for estimated quantity or none at all was objected to for destroying definite character; recommended language reserves right to make additional orders provided additional orders do not exceed twice the estimated quantity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge Advocate General recommended changing indefinite reservation to a definite cap: additional orders shall not exceed twice the estimated quantity. (C. 18164, July 6, 1905.)
